thread:
taylor_pm: Heads-up — Fjord Health's on-prem SI cutover failed during AzureGov marketplace attestation. They reported an attestation rejection plus a missing kernel UVM module.

elliot_marketplace: Oof. Can you paste the exact attestation error and the marketplace image tag/digest? we need to know if it's our attestor rejecting or Azure side.

taylor_pm: customer supplied: `registry://redwood-marketplace/edge-gw:2026-03-12a` attestation log: `ATTEST_ERROR: verification_failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (issuer CN=Fjord Internal CA)` also node log: `modprobe nvidia_uvm: FATAL: Module not found`.

sam_infra: two separate heads: (1) image attestation/CA chain, (2) driver/UVM on RHEL nodes. I'll prep a rollback manifest to the last known-good digest and test the pin in staging. Will share one-liner to patch.

maya_fieldeng: I'm on the call with Lina (Fjord ops) now — she confirmed nodes are RHEL 8.6 with custom DKMS and they didn't compile the UVM module when installing the NVIDIA driver. We can either walk them through building UVM or advise to install the vendor driver bundle that includes it.

nate_security: Quick look at the attestation blob: the signing intermediate is a customer-owned CA not present in our attestor trust list. Options: 1) ask customer to upload CA to Azure Attestation/marketplace flow, 2) add a temporary allowlist entry scoped to this deployment (audit required), or 3) require them to use a CA we already trust. Given this is AzureGov, we must be careful — option 2 needs signed sign-off with expiration and audit logs.

ellot_marketplace: (cc @alex_partner_mgr) we may need to loop in the marketplace partner manager to validate if gov tenant policies prevent adding external CA temporarily. alex?

alex_partner_mgr: I'm available. AzureGov tenant policies are stricter; temporary customer CA allowlist is tricky but feasible if we coordinate with Microsoft marketplace ops. I'll open a partner escalation and request a scoped exception for this SI deployment. Need ticket + artifact.

taylor_pm: OK action list: 1) sam prepare rollback pin and test in staging; 2) nate draft temporary allowlist approval language; 3) maya guide customer to build UVM or provide a driver bundle; 4) alex escalate with Azure marketplace ops. Scheduling a 30m triage at 16:00 PT — can everyone make it?

sam_infra: I can do 16:00 PT. prepping rollback. One-liner to pin (example):
```
kubectl -n redwood patch deployment edge-gw -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"edge-gw","image":"registry://redwood-marketplace/edge-gw@sha256:1111deadbeef2222"}]}}}}'
```
I'll verify healthchecks afterwards.

maya_fieldeng: I ran through quick steps with Lina — she can run `dkms autoinstall` and the `nvidia-modprobe --create-uvm` helper, but needs exact driver version. Their dkms shows `nvidia/470.182.03` installed but no uvm. I'll send an install snippet.

nate_security: Draft approval: "Security approves a timeboxed allowlist for Fjord Internal CA for the Fjord Health deployment only. Conditions: expires in 48 hours, entry logged in ticket INC-48721, full CA chain archived to secure customer folder, and immediate revoke if any anomalous attestation results observed." Adding to ticket.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: #INC-48721 - "FjordHealth: AzureGov attestation fail + on-prem driver UVM missing" assigned to partnerships@redwood. Priority: P1 for go-live.

taylor_pm: Also attaching attestation blob and CA subject/fingerprint into the ticket: `SHA1: 5f:2a:9c:33:7b:...` Lina is OK with temporary canary if we can guarantee rollback.

alex_partner_mgr: Escalation opened with Microsoft. They requested the attestation error, the CA chain (PEM), and the marketplace manifest digest. I'll update this thread when they respond.

sam_infra: rollback patched in staging and smoke tests green. I'll hold the patch ready to apply to prod if needed; ETA for apply if required ~30m.

maya_fieldeng: customer ran `dkms autoinstall` and then rebooted one node; `lsmod` now shows `nvidia_uvm`. Lina will finish the cluster rebuild overnight for remaining nodes.

nate_security: Microsoft responded: gov tenant will not accept unknown CA without marketplace ops exception. Alex, thanks for opening the case. Security recommends proceeding with the temporary allowlist for canary only while Azure ops issues an exception for the production rollout.

taylor_pm: Decision: allow temporary canary with allowlist + rollback guardrails. Sam, please hold prod patch until we confirm Azure ops exception or customer rekeys to trusted CA. Maya, track node rebuild; Lina to confirm when 100% nodes show uvm.

deploy-bot: Update on #INC-48721: triage complete. Next update expected 2026-03-12T20:00:00Z.

elliot_marketplace: Thanks team. Please dump any final logs into the ticket and ping me if the prod canary is executed so I can monitor attestation metrics.

taylor_pm: Closing loop here — will send a short summary to Fjord and schedule a postmortem if the rollback is triggered. :+1:
